newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia closes kindergartens after virus outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia closes kindergartens after virus outbreak.

text.p: Kindergarten schools in the Malaysian town of Sibu have been ordered to close following an outbreak of a potentially lethal strain of an airborne disease, the Bernama news agency said on Friday.

At least 17 children under the age of four have died of a new strain of the Coxsackie B virus since April, including two on Thursday. At least 15 children were in an isolation ward of the general hospital in Sibu, a coastal town in Sarawak state on Borneo.
Bernama quoted Sarawak Education Department director Putit Matzen Bernama as saying the decision to close the kindergartens was made on the advice of the state's health department.
Headmasters of primary schools in the affected areas should decide whether to close down the first three grades of their schools as well, Putit said.

The Coxsackie B virus has also struck children in the state capital of Kuching and Sarikei in Sarawak. Health Minister Chua Jui Meng said on Friday that children in the affected areas should remain at home even after the start of the new school term next week. He advised them to stay away from other places where small children gather. The virus, which can be transmitted by air, was orginally found in infected food, health officials have said. Symptoms include fever, nervous fits, paralysis and finally heart failure.
The Malaysian government had earlier turned to the Internet asking for help in tackling the spread of the disease.
